text_blocks.snippet: The side effects of Jardiance (empagliflozin) range from mild, common reactions to rare, life-threatening complications.

list.snippet: Increased urination and thirst: Passing more urine, larger volumes, and waking up at night because the drug removes excess glucose through the kidneys.
Urinary tract infections (UTIs): Symptoms include a burning sensation during urination, frequent urge, or cloudy/bloody urine.
Genital yeast infections: Common in both women and men, featuring itching, burning, redness, or thick white discharge.
Dehydration and low blood pressure: Fluid loss can cause dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting (especially when standing up).
Other mild effects: Nausea, joint pain, upper respiratory tract infections, or mild weight loss.

Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA): A dangerous buildup of acid in the blood that can happen even if your blood sugar is under 250 mg/dL. Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, tiredness, fruity breath odor, and trouble breathing.
Necrotizing fasciitis (Fournier's gangrene): A rare, life-threatening bacterial infection of the tissue in the perineum (between the anus and genitals) causing intense pain, swelling, and redness.
Pyelonephritis or urosepsis: Serious kidney or urinary infections spreading from the tract.
Low blood sugar (Hypoglycemia): More likely if Jardiance is taken alongside insulin or sulfonylureas.
Lower limb amputations: An increased risk of toe or leg amputation, particularly for patients with a history of vascular disease, foot ulcers, or prior amputation.
Serious allergic reactions: Swelling of the face, lips, or throat, hives, or trouble breathing.
